edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Ἐὰν δέ τις ἰουδαϊσμὸν ἑρμηνεύῃ ὑμῖν, μὴ ἀκούετε αὐτοῦ. ἄμεινον γάρ ἐστιν παρὰ ἀνδρὸς περιτομὴν ἔχοντος χριστιανισμὸν ἀκούειν, ἢ παρὰ ἀκροβύστου ἰουδαῖσμόν. ἐὰν δὲ ἀμφότεροι περὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ μὴ λαλῶσιν, οὗτοι ἐμοὶ στῆλαί εἰσιν καὶ τάφοι νεκρῶν, ἐφ̓ οἷς γέγραπται μόνον ὀνόματα ἀνθρώπων. [2] φεύγετε οὖν τὰς κακοτεχνίας καὶ ἐνέδρας τοῦ ἄρχοντος τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου, μήποτε θλιβέντες τῇ γνώμῃ αὐτοῦ ἐξασθενήσετε ἐν τῇ ἀγάπῃ: ἀλλὰ πάντες ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ γίνεσθε ἐν ἀμερίστῳ καρδίᾳ. [3] εὐχαριστῶ δὲ τῷ θεῷ μου, ὅτι εὐσυνείδητός εἰμι ἐν ὑμῖν καὶ οὐκ ἔχει τις καυχήσασθαι οὔτε λάθρα οὔτε φανερῶς, ὅτι ἐβάρησά τινα ἐν μικρῷ ἢ ἐν μεγάλῳ. καὶ πᾶσι δέ, ἐν οἷς ἐλάλησα, εὔχομαι, ἵνα μὴ εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτὸ κτήσωνται.
pass_a_gloss: But if anyone expounds Judaism to you, do not listen to him. For it is better to hear Christianity from a man who is circumcised than Judaism from one who is uncircumcised. But if neither of them speaks about Jesus Christ, they are to me tombstones and graves of the dead, on which only the names of men are written. Flee, then, the evil arts and traps of the ruler of this age, lest, crushed by his scheming, you grow weak in love; but all of you come together in one place with an undivided heart. And I thank my God that I have a clear conscience regarding you, and no one can boast, either in secret or openly, that I was a burden to anyone in small things or in great. And I pray for all among whom I spoke, that they may not come to have it as a testimony against them.
pass_b_english: If anyone explains Judaism to you, do not listen to him. Better to hear Christianity from a circumcised man than Judaism from an uncircumcised one. But if neither speaks of Jesus Christ, to me they are grave markers and tombs of the dead, carved with nothing but human names.
So run from the tricks and ambushes of the ruler of this age, or his schemes may press you hard and your love grow weak. Come together, all of you, with an undivided heart.

I thank my God that my conscience is clear toward you. No one can boast, privately or publicly, that I ever weighed on anyone, in a small matter or a great one. And for all those I spoke to, I pray that it will not become a testimony against them.

choices.english: grave markers and tombs of the dead
choices.why: στήλη is an inscribed stone slab; the image is a name on a tomb with no life behind it.
Expounding or interpreting Judaism, not preaching law.

choices.english: his schemes may press you hard
choices.why: θλίβω is pressure or affliction; γνώμη his purpose or design.
Being a financial or personal burden.

anf_compare.notes: Same sense. ANF 'preach the Jewish law' narrows ἑρμηνεύῃ ἰουδαϊσμόν (expound Judaism); 'conquered by his artifices' loosens θλιβέντες τῇ γνώμῃ.

notes: 'Ruler of this age' may echo John 12:31 or 1 Corinthians 2:6 (ἀρχόντων τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου); stock phrase in Ignatius, not cited inline.
'Burden' may echo 2 Corinthians 11:9; not cited inline.
Source shows 'ἐφ̓' with a variant breathing mark; reproduced as supplied.

review.notes: Paragraph [1] is Ignatius, Philadelphians 6: Judaism/Christianity, steles, the ruler, conscience, burden, and the prayer are all represented. Pass A keeps 'ἐφ̓ οἷς γέγραπται μόνον ὀνόματα ἀνθρώπων' as 'on which only the names of men are written' and 'ἵνα μὴ εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτὸ κτήσωνται' as hearers who 'may not come to have it'. Pass B 'carved with nothing but human names' is idiomatic for an inscribed στήλη and is not the fail. No inline citation is wrong; the notes rightly leave the stock echoes uncited. Title names the stele thought, not only the locus.
reasons: Pass B reverses agency in the prayer. Locked Greek 'ἵνα μὴ εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτὸ κτήσωνται' has the hearers as subject of κτήσωνται (they must not acquire it as a testimony). Pass A preserves that: 'they may not come to have it as a testimony against them'. Pass B 'it will not become a testimony against them' makes 'it' the subject and replaces acquiring with becoming.

The same clause shifts the relative. Greek 'καὶ πᾶσι δέ, ἐν οἷς ἐλάλησα, εὔχομαι' and Pass A 'And I pray for all among whom I spoke' mean among whom (ἐν οἷς); Pass B 'And for all those I spoke to, I pray' changes that to address.

review.notes: Source paragraph 1: Greek text matches Ignatius Philadelphians 6 (Lake 1912 Loeb). Pass A and B convey all clauses without omission, addition, or contradiction. Negation (μὴ ἀκούετε), agency (τις ἑρμηνεύῃ, ἀκούειν, λαλῶσιν), modality (ἔστιν, μὴ λαλῶσιν, εὔχομαι), and doctrine (contrast of circumcision/uncircumcised in Christ) preserved. Scripture: no inline citations in Greek, so none required; notes correctly identify possible allusions as unwritten. Title 'Grave Markers with Names' reflects thought of στῆλαι καὶ τάφοι νεκρῶν with γέγραπται μόνον ὀνόματα ἀνθρώπων. Covered source paragraphs: [1]. No uncertainties; all checks pass.
